DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, EDUCATION, AND WELFARE
OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY
WASHINGTON, D.C. 20201
MAY 17 1971
Mr. Charles J. Orlebeke
Deputy Under Secretary
Department of Housing and Urban Development
Washington, D. C. 20410
Dear Mr. Orlebeke:
Thank you for the opportunity to comment on the potential environmental impact of HUD's Operation Breakthrough. This attempt to improve housing technology and the neighborhood environment relates directly to two concerns of this Department: the physical, mental, and social health of the individual in his surroundings, and the cost, quality and durability of homes available to those of low and moderate incomes, many of who are recipients of public assistance.
In general, my saff and I have no adverse comments about the draft statement. Your emphasis on comprehensive planning and on careful monitoring of environment effects is particularly commendable.
There is, however, one missing element which is important, if any of your Breakthrough sites are to be true tests of the ability of varied income groups to live together. That missing element is some kind of training process, to teach people how to use their new Breakthrough homes and, more important, how to maintain them.
I also wonder how Breakthrough can be useful in an area of serious need--the renovation of units in urban areas. All of the sites mentioned in your draft are already vacant, and most are fairly large. I realize these conditions were necessary to demonstrate the potentials of industrialized housing.
